pillar_reactions.evidence: Re-delivered from the start in this second recording after the connection drop — custom programme from an onboarding call, plus 5 to 15 minutes of daily mobility aimed at stiffness and stabiliser strength. Asked for questions she said 'No. No? I got it.' She had already engaged enthusiastically with the mobility content in the first recording, so this was confirmation rather than fresh reaction. Her only intervention was to recommend the rep take ginkgo biloba for his memory.

The only prospect in the batch to interrogate the fasting recommendation on physiological grounds rather than practical ones: 'Is it good? Is it bad? Is it women shouldn't fast? Should they? Is it healthy for women? It's good for men, but is it good for women?' She backed it with a cautionary example — a cousin who water-fasted for 40 days, cleared several undiagnosed conditions and had to be refed on juices. The answer she got was observational rather than evidenced: 'at least from what I've seen with the women he works with, it's typically a little bit lighter. So maybe instead of eight hours, it's like 12 hours.' She accepted it and asked nothing further.

Delivered as weekly check-ins, programme updates, Trevor's personal number, outreach on missed workouts, plus group classes and coaching calls. She responded 'Nothing ready. Everything's pretty clear' and her only substantive comment on the whole delivery model was about the app: 'now apps do a lot... you can track a lot easier people and yourself through an app.' Flat acceptance — she had already said she does not need chasing, and this pillar is the weakest fit for her.

anchors.raw: I had a guy who did kickboxing, right? That was his specialty. And he was also a nutritionist. So he set up the diet, exercise and all that. And of course, we did it in person because we were in the same city... But I didn't really see any results.
anchors.competitor: A previous in-person coach and nutritionist in Europe
anchors.note: The most concrete undercut on this call — she has already paid a qualified professional for a superior delivery format, in person and in the same city, and got nothing. It makes remote asynchronous coaching a harder sell rather than an easier one, and the playbook's burned-before move was never used against it.

anchors.raw: usually, one-on-one coaching is pretty pricey... I knew it's not going to be [cheap], right? Because it is one-on-one. It is his time. I get it. I absolutely get it.
anchors.note: She arrived with a correct mental model of what one-to-one coaching costs and accepted the legitimacy of the number immediately, without a flicker of resistance to its fairness. The failure was capacity, not perceived value — she never disputed that $6,000 was the right price for what was described.

anchors.raw: as being a single mom with two boys, I do have to put it in [perspective]
anchors.note: The binding constraint. She is funding a household of three from her own practice, and her specific fear was not the total but the risk of committing to six months and having to stop at two or three. That is an argument for a shorter or pausable tier, and none exists.

anchors.raw: In the meantime, I'll just stick with his videos.
anchors.note: Her stated fallback is the free content that brought her in, which she has followed for six months and already trains from. The programme's own marketing is its closest substitute for this buyer, and nothing in the call differentiated the paid product against it.

unmet_demand.want: A clear, evidenced position on whether fasting and the rest of the protocol are appropriate for a 50-year-old woman
unmet_demand.why_unmet: She asked directly and received an answer drawn entirely from what the rep had noticed among Trevor's female clients, with an improvised twelve-hour window offered as the female version of a ten-hour one. There is no stated female protocol, no evidence base referenced, and no clinician in the loop.

unmet_demand.want: A commitment shape she could safely afford — something shorter, pausable, or with a defined exit if her budget changed
unmet_demand.why_unmet: She articulated this precisely as her concern about starting and having to stop after two or three months. The offer is six months minimum with no pause mechanism and no stated policy for a client who cannot continue, and no alternative structure was quoted despite two hints that alternatives existed.

unmet_demand.want: Reassurance that this would not repeat her previous coaching failure
unmet_demand.why_unmet: She named the fear and its history and got a two-word answer. No proof, no case study, no guarantee mentioned on this call, and no use of the playbook's scripted response to exactly this objection.

unmet_demand.want: To know what the actual options were after hearing she could not afford the headline price
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep twice signalled that other routes existed and quoted none. She left the call believing there might be a way she never heard, which is a worse outcome for both sides than a straight no would have been.
